# Import-ZbxConfiguration

## SYNOPSIS

Imports a configuration document into the server.

## SYNTAX

### Path (Default)

```
Import-ZbxConfiguration [-Path] <string[]> [-Format <ZabbixConfigurationFormat>] -Rules <ZabbixConfigurationImportRuleRequest> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Text

```
Import-ZbxConfiguration -Source <string> [-Format <ZabbixConfigurationFormat>] -Rules <ZabbixConfigurationImportRuleRequest> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### LiteralPath

```
Import-ZbxConfiguration -LiteralPath <string[]> [-Format <ZabbixConfigurationFormat>] -Rules <ZabbixConfigurationImportRuleRequest> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Import-ZbxConfiguration cmdlet applies a configuration document (text, or files with -Path, which takes wildcards, or -LiteralPath) in JSON, XML or YAML (-Format, else a file's extension, else the text's first character) with configuration.import, creating or changing the hosts, templates, groups, maps, media types and other objects it holds. -Rules says, for each kind of object, whether the import creates what is missing, updates what exists and deletes what the document leaves out. Compare-ZbxConfiguration shows what an import would change first. It asks for confirmation unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Restore a deleted template from an export

```powershell
$backup = Export-ZbxConfiguration -Template 'Web App' -Format Yaml
Remove-ZbxTemplate -InputObject 'Web App' -Confirm:$false
$backup | Import-ZbxConfiguration -Format Yaml -Rules @{
    Templates = @{ CreateMissing = $true }
    Items     = @{ CreateMissing = $true }
} -Confirm:$false | Out-Null
Get-ZbxTemplate -Name 'Web App' | Select-Object TemplateId, TechnicalName
```

-Rules says what each object family may do (the typed rules of configuration.import; a hashtable casts to it). An import always asks for a second confirmation, so a script passes -Confirm:$false (or -Force).

### Example 2: Put a host back the way a file describes it

```powershell
$path = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) 'web-01.yaml'
Export-ZbxConfiguration -Host 'web-01' -Path $path
Set-ZbxHost 'web-01' -Description 'changed by hand' | Out-Null
Import-ZbxConfiguration -Path $path -Rules @{ Hosts = @{ UpdateExisting = $true } } -Confirm:$false | Out-Null
Get-ZbxHost -Name 'web-01' | Select-Object TechnicalName, Description
Remove-Item $path
```

-Path reads the document from a file, in the format its extension names (.yaml here, as Export-ZbxConfiguration wrote it). UpdateExisting overwrites the host's current settings with the file's.

### Example 3: Preview an import

```powershell
Export-ZbxConfiguration -Host 'web-01' | Import-ZbxConfiguration -Rules @{ Hosts = @{ UpdateExisting = $true } } -WhatIf
```

-WhatIf names the document without sending it; Compare-ZbxConfiguration shows what would change.
